KuaiRec2: When a candidate's title or category matches a topic that the user has previously completed (watched at least half the duration), prefer it; if the user consistently skipped similar topics, avoid it.
Candidates with high engagement ratios (likes/plays > 5% or comments/plays > 1%) are more likely to be chosen, especially when they also match the user's historical category preferences.
If a candidate belongs to a category frequently skipped in the user's history (e.g., 时尚/营销售卖/女装, 自拍 with low engagement), deprioritize it unless other strong signals exist.
For users with many followers or role Video Author, prefer candidates with high absolute engagement (plays > 1M or likes > 50k) and avoid low-engagement content.
If the user has a history of completing videos with emotional or heartwarming content (民生资讯/暖新闻, 情感/亲密关系), prefer candidates in those categories over pure entertainment or lifestyle.
When a candidate is a duplicate or near-duplicate of a previously skipped item, avoid it; otherwise, for new items, rely on category match and engagement.
goodreads: When the user has read and highly rated multiple volumes of a specific series, prefer the next unread volume in that same series over unrelated high-rated options.

Prefer fantasy/paranormal or mystery/thriller/crime graphic novels over non-fiction or historical biography titles, unless the history tag co-occurs with fantasy or the user has rated similar historical graphic memoirs highly.

Do not default to widely popular superhero or classic titles (e.g., Watchmen, Persepolis, Calvin and Hobbes) merely for high ratings; the user shows mixed engagement with superheroes and strong engagement with quirky indie fantasy series.
If the user's recent reads cluster around a single series or author, and a candidate belongs to that series while others do not, favor the series continuation.

When candidates include a first volume of a series matching the user's demonstrated taste for humorous/indie fantasy (e.g., Rat Queens, Saga, Lumberjanes style), prefer it over generic superhero team-up or single-issue titles.

Prefer candidates with a substantial number of ratings and moderate-to-high average rating over obscure low-rating-count titles, unless the obscure title continues a series the user is actively reading.
mobilerec: When the user's history shows strong engagement with games (rating 4-5 on multiple games across action, strategy, puzzle, or arcade), prefer a game candidate over a non-game candidate even if a non-game has higher apparent utility.

When the user's history contains ratings of 5 on dating or social apps and the candidates include a dating/social app, that dating app is a plausible pick, but do not default to finance or banking apps for such users.

Do not assume users with finance/banking history (ratings 4-5 on finance apps) will prefer another finance app; often they select a game or content app instead, so treat finance candidates as low priority unless other signals point to it.

When a user has rated medical or health apps highly (4-5) and also shows productivity/tool usage, they may pick a brain/puzzle or wellness-adjacent app; prefer functional puzzle/word candidates over medical utility duplicates.

Users who rate many apps low (1-2) for bugs, ads, or paywalls tend to pick simple, high-rated, low-friction candidates (puzzle, casual, word, or clean utility) rather than complex RPG/strategy titles.
When the user's history is sparse or mixed, prefer the candidate with the highest rating and broadest appeal (e.g., mainstream puzzle/word/casual) over niche simulation, AR, or low-review apps.
